title: How Diago works
summary: A source-grounded map of Diago: how its agent guidance and local tools turn scoped engineering evidence into validated, standalone diagrams. Choose a perspective, inspect a component, then follow its cited sources. Diago does not independently prove that cited claims are true.

components.label: Coding assistant
components.description: Uses the task-matched Diago skill and local tools to create a diagram for an engineering question. The host agent is responsible for inspecting available sources and assessing the claims.

components.label: Diago skills
components.description: Guide source inspection, view selection, evidence labeling, authoring, rendering, and diagram review. They are instructions for the host agent, not background workers.

components.label: Selected source scope
components.description: Repository code, contracts, task statements, or conversation context inspected by the host agent for the requested diagram. Diago does not scan an arbitrary repository on its own.

components.label: Diago CLI
components.description: Local commands for advice, plans, validation, rendering, Explorer output, evidence-workflow review, health checks, and examples.

components.label: Local MCP server
components.description: Exposes Diago's tools over the local stdio Model Context Protocol transport. It is not a hosted API.

components.label: MCP tool dispatcher
components.description: Validates structured tool inputs and calls the same local recommendation, planning, validation, and rendering modules used by the command line.

components.label: View advisor
components.description: Ranks authored diagram recipes against the engineering question and returns a renderer, profile, rationale, scope, and complexity budget. It does not inspect repository files.

components.label: Plan and review
components.description: Creates a bounded schema-v2 plan and checks its evidence lanes, renderer fit, complexity, and fidelity before diagram authoring.

components.label: Diagram JSON
components.description: Compact semantic input authored by the host agent. Specialized diagram documents and the multi-view Explorer document have distinct schemas.

components.label: Renderer catalog
components.description: Defines eleven specialized output types, their reader questions, supported profiles, renderer engines, and complexity limits.

components.label: Validation boundary
components.description: Checks schemas, references, evidence links, renderer constraints, accessibility, and complexity. A present citation is not independent proof of factual truth.

components.label: Renderer registry
components.description: Validates a diagram and routes it to the pinned Archify renderer or a native Diago adapter according to the catalog.

components.label: Bundled Archify
components.description: The bundled renderer for Architecture, Sequence, Workflow, Dataflow, and Lifecycle diagrams. Diago adds its shared presentation and review controls around this renderer.

components.label: Native Diago renderers
components.description: Six Diago-owned adapters render Data model, Timeline, Layers, Dependency, Security matrix, and Fishbone outputs.

components.label: Explorer composer
components.description: Validates shared-component, multi-perspective input and composes one standalone Explorer artifact.

components.label: Evidence workflow helper
components.description: Plans bounded work over a caller-supplied evidence snapshot and retains conflicts and failures. It does not fetch sources, launch workers, or verify claims independently.

components.label: Standalone HTML artifact
components.description: A local HTML file with its renderer, styles, and interaction logic embedded. MCP render calls return a compact path and integrity receipt, not the full HTML in the conversation.
